cards.text: Friend, Jeremiah the prophet is still bringing the LORD's message about Babylon, and it is NOT getting any softer. This is what the LORD says: 'Behold, I will stir up against Babylon and against the people of Leb-kamai…' Now, when I hear 'stir up,' I picture a big bowl of cookie dough, and I have a feeling this is NOT cookie dough.

cards.question: Against Babylon and the people of Leb-kamai, what does the LORD say He will stir up?

cards.text: And there's more, friend. The LORD says He'll send strangers to Babylon to winnow her and empty her land in her day of disaster.

cards.question: The strangers the LORD sends will come at Babylon from just one direction.

cards.text: From EVERY side, so Babylon goes looking for the back door and it's ALL front door. Then come the battle orders: do not let the archer bend his bow or put on his armor, and devote all her army to destruction.

cards.question: The battle orders say this about Babylon's young men: do not ___ them.

cards.text: Her army will fall slain in the land of the Chaldeans, pierced through in her streets. And then, right in the middle of all this, the LORD says something about Israel and Judah.

cards.question: In the middle of the battle orders against Babylon, what does the LORD say about Israel and Judah?

answers.text: Their God has not abandoned them
Their land is free of all guilt

cards.text: Not abandoned, even though their land is full of guilt before the Holy One of Israel. Friend, I spent YEARS forgotten in the back of a junk drawer, so 'not abandoned' gets me RIGHT in the apron.
Then the call goes out: 'Flee from Babylon! Escape with your lives! Do not be destroyed in her punishment.'

cards.question: Why the big rush to get out of Babylon?

answers.text: It is the time of the LORD's vengeance
Her great river is about to flood
Her king has ordered everyone out

cards.text: Then the prophet paints a picture. Babylon was a gold cup in the hand of the LORD.

cards.question: Babylon, the gold cup in the hand of the LORD, made the whole earth ___.
The nations drank Babylon's wine and came away clear-headed.

cards.text: Then, suddenly, Babylon has fallen and been shattered. Somebody calls out: wail for her, get her balm for her pain, perhaps she can be healed.

cards.question: When they try to heal shattered Babylon, she recovers.

cards.text: She could not be healed, so the word is: abandon her, everybody go back to your own land, because her judgment reaches all the way to the clouds. That's the repair guy taking ONE look under the hood, sliding your keys back across the counter, and saying, 'Friend… just go home.'

cards.question: Then comes the call: the LORD has brought our vindication, so come, let's tell what the LORD our God has accomplished. Tell it where?

cards.text: Now the orders get LOUD: 'Sharpen the arrows! Fill the quivers!' And the LORD Himself has stirred up someone's spirit to come against Babylon.

cards.question: Against Babylon, whose spirit has the LORD stirred up?
The LORD's plan is aimed at Babylon to destroy her, and it is the vengeance of the LORD, vengeance for His ___.

cards.text: Then: raise a banner against the walls of Babylon, post the guard, station the watchmen, prepare the ambush. Friend, that's FOUR jobs in one breath, and I can't get my oven preheated and my timer set at the same time.

cards.question: The LORD has both planned and carried out what He spoke against the people of Babylon.

cards.text: Then Babylon hears it straight: you who dwell by many waters, rich in treasures, your end has come. Rich… comfortable… waterfront property… and then, the thread of your life is cut.

cards.question: Then the LORD of Hosts swears an oath against Babylon. What does He swear by?
The LORD swears He will fill Babylon with men, as with locusts, and they will shout in triumph over her.

cards.text: Then the prophecy turns to the LORD Himself: He made the earth by His power, and when He thunders, the waters in the heavens roar and He brings the wind out of His storehouses. Friend, I've got ONE oven and a timer that beeps at me, and the LORD keeps WIND in STOREHOUSES.

Now put the idols next to that: every goldsmith is put to shame by his idols, because his molten images are a fraud. Friend, I'm a cookie stamper who got sold for a quarter, and even I know better than to call myself a god.

cards.question: Next to the LORD who brings the wind, those molten images have no ___ in them.

cards.text: The idols are worthless, a work to be mocked, and in the time of their punishment they will perish. But the Portion of Jacob, the LORD of Hosts, is not like these.

cards.question: Why is the Portion of Jacob not like those idols?

answers.text: He is the Maker of all things
He lives high above the clouds
He sits in a bigger temple

cards.text: Then the LORD speaks to someone and says, 'You are My war club, My weapon for battle.' He doesn't say who, and He just keeps going.

cards.question: What does the LORD say He does with His war club?

cards.text: Then the list rolls on, one 'with you I shatter' after another: horse and rider, chariot and driver, man and woman, old and young, shepherd and flock, farmer and oxen, governors and officials. Friend, the LORD says it so many times you can feel the drumbeat.

cards.question: Still speaking to His war club, the LORD says He will repay Babylon and everyone in Chaldea before the war club's very eyes. Repay them for what?

answers.text: All the evil they did in Zion
All the gold they took from Egypt
All the towers they built too high

cards.text: Then the LORD says, 'Behold, I am against you, O destroying mountain…' He will stretch out His hand, roll it over the cliffs, and turn it into a charred mountain.

cards.question: Someday someone will pull a cornerstone out of the destroying mountain the LORD is against, to build with again.

cards.text: And that's where we'll set the timer for now, friend. Trust me, this message about Babylon is still baking.

findings.problem: Discovery and luck-based questions occur too often across both stops, rather than remaining a few exceptions among mostly informed guesses. For example, the earlier cards give no basis for reasoning out the attackers' direction (stop 1, card 4), what the LORD says about Israel and Judah (stop 1, card 8), where to tell the news (stop 1, card 18), which kings are stirred up (stop 2, card 2), what the LORD swears by (stop 2, card 7), or the content of the locust oath (stop 2, card 8). The setups commonly withhold a fact and immediately ask for it.

rule.text: A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

findings.problem: The card tells verse 4, but its second sentence also uses verse 5 when it says that the LORD then says something about Israel and Judah. The citation therefore ends one verse too early.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The setup says only that Babylon was a gold cup. It does not supply the wine or drinking imagery needed to reason out 'drunk,' so the baker is supplying an unseen word from the line; 'rich' is also a plausible guess from the gold imagery.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: Nothing in the earlier cards points to the temple as the reason for this vengeance. The blank therefore asks the baker to guess the next wording of the prophetic line rather than reason out its meaning from the setup.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.
